claims.text: High-entropy alloys have complex, chemically disordered atomic structures.
The high-entropy alloys under consideration are used in thermal-insulation applications.
Coupling a disorder-sensitive interatomic potential to advanced phonon-transport solvers will significantly improve lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy.
The proposed potential will explicitly capture local chemical fluctuations and force-constant variations.
Conventional ab initio or empirical approaches do not fully account for atomic-disorder complexity in HEAs.
Local chemical fluctuations are related to lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy materials.
Chemical disorder in HEAs produces mass and force-constant fluctuations that affect phonon dynamics.
Force-constant fluctuations increase phonon attenuation or scattering and reduce phonon lifetimes.
Local bonding variations change phonon mean free paths.
Disorder or lattice distortion can lower lattice thermal conductivity by reducing phonon velocity and increasing phonon scattering.
More refined modeling of atomic-scale disorder will reduce uncertainty in phonon-scattering predictions relative to conventional models.
The approach is applicable to HEAs with moderate to high atomic disorder and force-constant fluctuations.
The approach is applicable only in temperature regimes where phonon scattering dominates heat conduction.
The approach will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error by at least approximately 20% relative to disorder-insensitive methods.
The approach will more reliably identify HEAs with intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach may not improve predictions for alloys with very low disorder.
Extremely amorphous systems outside the model's calibrated regime may not be predicted reliably.
Inelastic neutron scattering or laser-flash analysis can be used to obtain the required experimental lattice-thermal-conductivity benchmark.
Failure to reduce prediction error by at least approximately 20% relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
